blind.why: Ours is m_mid (setView 'mid'). Its shaded floor is a saturated cobalt (avg RGB 33,56,89, B/R 2.7) while shaded walls are warm brown (100,83,68), so the palette splits in two and the shadow reads as blue paint, not shade. CS2 Mirage shade is a warm neutral (69,58,52), with layered cast-shadow detail and form on every surface.

Ours is m_b-tunnel. A fully roofed tunnel is lit as flat as open air. The floor (34,52,79) matches open-sky shadow and the ceiling (88,53,22) is brighter than the walls (65,50,38). There are no light pools, no darkening with depth and no sky occlusion. CS2's underpass has dark covered zones, shaped light patches and clear depth.

Ours is m_hub-arches. It is clean and readable but flat: a huge uniformly lit floor, walls with little form shading and weak contrast between lit and shaded walls. A blue band sits along the shaded edges and the sky is oversaturated. CS2 Italy has strong value structure, aerial depth and a cohesive grade.

biggest_gap: The ambient/shadow term is wrong. Surfaces outside the sun take an unoccluded, oversaturated blue sky term. Reproduce: ?test=1&seed=1&match=1, hide the HUD, then __game.ctx.map.debug.setView('mid' | 'long' | 'a-door' | 'b-tunnel'). (1) Open-air shadowed floors render cobalt (33,56,89) while shaded walls render brown, which breaks the palette. (2) The roofed B tunnel floor gets the same blue sky light as open air, and its ceiling is brighter than its walls. Fix: desaturate and warm the hemisphere/sky ambient so shade is roughly neutral with only a slight cool tint (CS2 shade ~69,58,52). Then occlude ambient and sky light by sky visibility: bake it into the existing bakeVertexAO colour attribute, or add per-zone light-probe or interior volumes, so covered areas such as tunnels, under catwalks and doorways are clearly darker and warmer, and add bounce from sunlit floors.
other_gaps: Low value range and contrast on vertical surfaces: a sunlit wall vs a shaded wall differs by only about 15-25% (a-door arch crop), so geometry reads flat and cardboard-like. CS2 runs about 3-4x lit/shade with strong form shading.

The sky is oversaturated near the zenith (pure electric blue at a-door and hub) with low-poly cartoon clouds. It clashes with the warm sand palette and gives no aerial-perspective gradient toward the horizon.

No visible interior or local lighting. The listed lamp and lightProbe zones (tunnel-a/b/c, catwalk-under) produce no light pools or accents in b-tunnel. Interiors need dark-to-light gradients and local warm sources.
Distant set pieces in B site (~30 m) wash out to a hazy, low-contrast pink/grey with weak cast shadows (the awning). Fog plus the bloom veil flattens depth instead of layering it.
Shadow-casting props are sparse and shadows are simple single-object shapes. Little shadow detail (lattices, beams, foliage), which CS2 uses heavily to give surfaces life.
Ground textures read as flat colour plus faint speckle at gameplay distance (sand, tile). No roughness or specular variation, so materials look like the same matte plastic.
bugs: Harness, not render: __game.place() is overridden during the buy phase (the actor snaps back to spawn at -8,0,45.5 within 0.1 s), and &phase=live with match=1 still reports phase 'buy'. Critics have to use map.debug.setView to inspect the map.
strengths: Zero console errors across the gallery, 7 map views and a quality switch
About 220-275 draw calls and 120-135k tris per map view, 11-12 post passes. Low preset (scale 0.85, 1024 shadows, 7 post calls) looks almost identical to high, so it scales gracefully
Clean MSAA/FXAA edges, stable texel-snapped sun shadows with crisp contact edges
Cohesive, readable stylised world from the cine-a overview; site and callout signage and team-colour accents read well
Gallery materials (glass, metal, emissive bloom, textured kinds) are distinct and work
